matters.body: REGULAR MEETING - FIRST TUESDAY - AFTERNOON & EVENING SESSIONS
matters.text:
Agenda Item Details 

 Meeting 
 Jan 02, 2024 - REGULAR MEETING - FIRST TUESDAY - AFTERNOON & EVENING SESSIONS 
 Category 
 K. REPORT AND RECOMMENDATION OF THE CITY MANAGER 
 Subject 
 1. Public Bid Waiver – Water Meter Install/Replacement-Electronic Water Meters and Supplies – Neptune Technology Group 
 Type 
 Action (Consent)

 Jan 02, 2024 
 Absolute Date 
 Jan 02, 2024 
 Fiscal Impact 
 Yes 
 Dollar Amount 
 4,400,000.00 
 Budgeted 
 Yes 
 Budget Source 
 Capital Improvement Program 
 Recommended Action 
 Authorize the waiver of standard bidding requirements for the equipment and services specified with Neptune Technology Group in an annual amount not to exceed $4,400,000. 

 Gregory Jenkins, Raleigh Water 

 Regarding General Statute 143-129 Raleigh Water is requesting to waive bidding requirements for water metering devices and equipment. The reasoning for this request coincides with section E(6) of the statute for “the standardization or compatibility” with current software, hardware, and the ability to easily maintain all appurtenances as the overriding consideration. The Raleigh Water AMR replacement project (2006-2008) approved on May 16 th , 2006, following an RFP and Public Bid, is nearing year 18 from the initial installation . The project consisted of replacing more than 155,000 analog meters and standardizing all the water meters across the City with Neptune AMR “Drive-By” Automated Metering Devices. 

 To date, Raleigh Water maintains more than 210,000 Neptune water meters. 160,000 of these meters have been replaced since 2015 and are now AMR/AMI capable smart meters. Neptune hardware allows for three types of reading capability: AMR “drive-by”, AMI “fixed network”, and cellular. Neptune’s water meters utilize proprietary software and do not require any additional re-programming or splicing when replacing older or damaged meters, which decreases the cost and labor for the installation and maintenance of the meters. 

 Neptune Technology group has won each open bid over the past 20 years due to competitive pricing, and simplicity of Hardware. Neptune meters are sourced directly from the manufacturer, eliminating third-party bidding increases. Additionally, one-source manufacturing standardizes equipment and eliminates logistical hardships with housing multiple metering devices and/or requiring the modification to the existing meter inventory for reading purposes. Raleigh Water installs on average 5,500 new meters annually due to ongoing development, a 20% increase in the past 2 years. On top of these additional meters is the replacement of approximately 13,000 meters annually due to “end-of-life” batteries. These “failures” have been trending down since 2020 at which time Raleigh Water experienced over 20,500 end-of-life meters. Projections show this number trending to approximately 10,000 meters annually in the coming years which shall continue as a needed replacement cycle for the foreseeable future aligning with the 20-year battery life now attained. Ongoing costs of system upkeep should account for a minimum of 16,000 meters annually to allow internal resources the ability to perform required maintenance and provide new metered services to customers without additional overtime needs. This effort eliminates mass replacements if battery life ends within a 3-year period as they did with the original project meters. 

 As per General Statute 143-129 (e)(6), the City Council may waive competitive bidding when other overriding considerations outweigh competitive bidding. Due to end-user ease in operation/maintenance, historical affordability, and standardized compatibility Neptune TG has submitted price estimates for Raleigh Water’s needed material in the amount of $4,400,000. Funds have been budgeted and will be encumbered under the Capital Improvement Program. 

 §

 Recommended Action 
 Authorize the City Manager to execute a contract with CITI, Inc. in the amount not to exceed $5,808,776. Authorize the associated budget transfer in an amount of $3,908,776. 

 Erika Bailey, Raleigh Water 

 In Fiscal Year 2024, Raleigh Water completed a Comprehensive Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and Controls Assessment Project to understand inventory, condition, obsolescence, and replacement needs at the Resource Recovery Facilities (RRFs) and remote lift stations. This project was a recommended asset management project identified in the 2023 Raleigh Water Integrated Master Plan. ​ 

 On March 20, 2024, the Resource Recovery Division received a proposal from its system integrator CITI, Inc. to convert all PLCs and associated hardware at the RRFs and remote lift stations to a new system platform based on findings from the assessment project. This project is similar to a PLC upgrade project recently completed at the water treatment plants. The PLCs are the primary components that make up the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition System (SCADA) for automated monitoring and control of the RRFs and associated lift stations. The PLC control system currently in use has production date ranges from 1997 to 2009 and is now obsolete and is no longer commercially available for direct replacement, nor do they receive technical support from the factory. 

 Staff is requesting a 5-year contract with CITI, Inc. in the amount of $5,808,776 for this upgrade project. Raleigh Water currently has $1,900,000 budgeted as part of its Capital Improvement Program for initial Resource Recovery Division PLC replacements. Because insufficient funds are currently available to cover all recommended upgrades, a budget transfer of $3,908,776 is needed. The availability of funds for transfer arises from the postponement of a sewer interceptor capacity expansion project, which was deemed unnecessary due to recent hydraulic modeling results showing that the existing interceptor size is adequately equipped to handle wet-weather design flows, contrary to earlier predictions. 

 On May 5, 2020, City Council authorized a service contract with CITI for SCADA services which included authorization to waive the standard bidding requirements for equipment and services specified with CITI for capital improvement contracts.

Agenda Item Details

 Recommended Action 
 Authorize the waiver of standard bidding requirements for the equipment and services specified from Qwake Technologies, Inc., and authorize the City Manager to execute the associated contract in the amount not to exceed $272,600. 

 J. K. Wilder, Fire

 The Raleigh Fire Department (RFD) has been chosen to be one of the first eighty fire departments in the United States to participate in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Science and Technology National Field Assessment (NFA); a program that makes innovative fire safety technology available to fire departments for real-world use and assessment. 

 The NFA is a three-week assessment of Qwake Technologies’ Navigator product and their innovative C-THRU technology, that offers significant ergonomic and life safety improvements on existing twenty-year-old thermal image camera technology (TIC). The older TIC technology is a hand-held tool that is limited to providing only sight and colored temperature variations, in a dark smoke-filled room. The Navigator is a hands-free, helmet-mounted visualization and navigation tool, that integrates with the user through heads up display. Each is capable of tracing the straight edges, curved edges and corners of items such as walls, interior furnishings and victims providing for a more accurate and faster identification of a firefighter’s surroundings and life safety priorities. Additionally, the Navigator is equipped with cellular services allowing for peer-to-peer communication and live streaming to incident commanders. This interactive communication provides means for information sharing that uniquely allows each Navigator on scene to map the structure, including exit pathways, on the heads up display. 

 Developed by Austin, Texas - based startup Qwake Technologies, Qwake’s C-THRU platform leverages augmented reality, intelligent sensors and proprietary visual language to support navigation and coordination of critical workers. This technology will enable the RFD to enhance firefighter safety, increase operational effectiveness and information sharing, and training for improved knowledge transfer and efficacy. 

 In advance of the NFA, the RFD was one of a select few departments to receive a half day of on-site demonstration and testing with Qwake. As a result, the RFD is purchasing 15 Navigator units that will be distributed for use by RFD front-line units in the community. 

 Since this is new technology only available through Qwake, RFD must purchase the C-THRU devices directly from Qwake and requests a public bid waiver to enter into a contract for the procurement of this equipment, including warranty and connectivity services. As per General Statute 143-129 (e)(6), the City Council may waive competitive bidding when a needed product is available from only one source of supply. 

 RFD is currently in a narrowed competitive process where Qwake will select ten fire departments to partner in the use and development of this groundbreaking technology. Perks of partnership status include concerted field testing of new technologies and discounted pricing and upgrades to newer technology as it becomes available. 

 §

 Recommended Action 
 Authorize the City Manager to execute a 10-year contract with DMT in the amount not to exceed $4,042,036 and approve the transfer in the amount of $112,000. 

 Erika Bailey, Raleigh Water 

 The Raleigh Water, Neuse River Resource Recovery Facility Bioenergy Recovery Project’s Digester Gas Treatment System (DGTS) is nearing construction completion and will soon be online for continuous operation. The complex instrumentation, mechanical, and electrical components necessary to ensure the high quality renewable natural gas standards are met necessitates award of a service maintenance agreement to ensure compliance in accordance with Renewable Natural Gas regulations required under the interconnect agreement between the City of Raleigh and Enbridge (formerly Dominion Energy). Proposals for the DGTS service maintenance agreement we re received in July of 2018. 
 Bids were requested from three suppliers named in the project technical specifications; two proposals were received on July 17, 2018 to furnish and deliver the Digester Gas Treatment System (DGTS) to the Neuse River Resource Recovery Facility (NRRRF) to treat the anaerobic digester biogas to meet utility-grade natural gas requirements. The scope of the project included shop testing, installation support, commissioning, performance testing, training, and an option for a service maintenance agreement. Under the Construction Manager at Risk procurement process, proposals were received and evaluated with the initially selected proposer failing to substantially agree to the terms and conditions of the agreement. As a result, the second-ranked proposer was recommended for award of the equipment purchase and to provide maintenance, operation, and monitoring services of the Digester Gas Treatment System. Although proposals were received in July 2018, the option to contract the additional annual service maintenance agreement was delayed as these would not be required until closer to completion of construction and commissioning of the equipment furnished by DMT. Due to the delay in the service agreement, modifications were negotiated with the supplier as recommended for award by City Staff. Additionally, this digester gas treatment system is a proprietary system designed and developed by DMT.

 Edward Buchan, Raleigh Water 

 The EM Johnson Water Treatment Plant utilizes a belt filter press process to dewater solids removed from the water treatment process. The solids produced through the dewatering process are classified as a “Class A” residual and are approved and beneficial for land application. The current dewatering belt presses have been in service for over 25 years and the mechanical wear items have reached their intended service life and need to be replaced. The dewatering belt presses will be equipped with updated technology and equipment that allows for higher throughput, increasing efficiency and productivity in dewatering operations. 

 Alfa Laval Incorporated is the Original Equipment Manufacturer of the Klampress Type 94/890 2.0-meter belt filter presses installed at E.M. Johnson Water Treatment Plant and is the sole source authorized provider for all Original Equipment Manufacturer parts and service. Only Alfa Laval Inc. certified personnel are allowed to install parts in order to preserve the equipment warranty. As per General Statute 143-129 (e)(6), the City Council may waive competitive bidding when other overriding considerations outweigh competitive bidding. Alfa Laval Incorporated has submitted an estimate for furnishing and integrating new dewatering belt presses in the amount of $ 737,415.00.

 Recommended Action 
 1) Authorize the waiver of standard bidding requirements for the materials and services specified with Schindler Elevator Corporation. 2) Authorize the City Manager to execute the contract with Schindler Elevator Corporation in the amount not to exceed $914,000. 3) Authorize associated budget transfers to fund the project. 

 Michelle Bradley, Raleigh Convention Center and Performing Arts Complex

 The Raleigh Convention and Performing Arts Complex (RCPAC) is in need of modernization and replacement of aging escalators due to wear from daily use. 
 A pressing concern is the escalators at the Meymandi Concert Hall, which were installed in 2001. Parts for these escalators are becoming obsolete, making maintenance increasingly difficult and posing potential risks to public safety and accessibility. Schindler is the original equipment manufacturer and current maintenance provider. 
 To ensure standardization and compatibility with the existing system, and considering Schindler's role as the original equipment manufacturer and maintenance provider, sole-source procurement via a Bid Waiver has been identified as the most appropriate course of action. This request encompasses the modernization work to be contracted separately from the ongoing maintenance agreement. This approach will ensure compliance and allow RCPAC to address the most pressing concerns first while still being able to maintain the seamless service and equipment integrity throughout the venues of RCPAC as a whole. 
 General Statute 143-129 (e)(6) provides that the City Council may waive competitive bidding requirements when standardization or compatibility is the overriding consideration in the selection of a vendor. Due to end-user ease in operation/maintenance, historical affordability, and standardized compatibility, staff is recommending to waive the competitive bidding requirements and contract with Schindler Elevator Corporation for this modernization work at an amount not to exceed $914,000. 

 §

 Budget Source 
 Operating Budget/Capital Improvement Program 
 Recommended Action 
 Authorize the waiver of standard bidding requirements for the procurement of powder activated carbon and award a contract to Arq, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $580,000. 

 Ed Buchan, Raleigh Water

 Powder Activated Carbon is a chemical used at the City’s (2) water treatment plants to remove taste and odor compounds, organics and per/polyfluorinated compounds (PFAS). To determine the most effective product at removing these contaminants, vendors provided a one-pound sample of their respective carbon products for analysis. Performance jar testing was conducted for both drinking water supply sources and the Arq, Inc TRA carbon product was selected based on overall performance and PFAS removal.

 Specifically, the Arq product was superior at reducing perfluorooctanesulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoate (PFOA) even at lower doses compared to the other products. Both PFOS and PFOA are regulated contaminants, with the Maximum Contaminant Level set at 4 parts per trillion for both compounds. The Arq, Inc. TRA carbon is a proprietary product, uniquely suited to the City’s source waters and will help ensure compliance with PFAS drinking water regulations.

 Pursuant to General Statute 143-129 (e)(6), the City Council may waive competitive bidding when a needed product is available from only one source of supply. The TRA carbon is only available from one supplier – Arc, Inc. In order maintain compliance with drinking water regulations for PFAS, it is recommended the TRA carbon product is selected and a contract awarded to Arq, Inc without a formal bidding process.

 §
